name: War Mission
definition: A military unit pursues a bounded objective inside a wider conflict where coordination, uncertainty, command, and moral injury complicate the meaning of success.
negative_signals: war used only as historical scenery
single duel detached from collective conflict
diagnostic_questions: Does the unit objective organize the action?
Do command and collective dependence create moral as well as tactical pressure?

neighbors.distinction: War mission may include rescue, but success is defined by a strategic objective in armed conflict.
War mission is shaped by military organization rather than frontier legitimacy.

reader_promises.name: Unit dependence
reader_promises.description: Make differentiated people rely on one another under operational pressure.

reader_promises.name: Costed objective
reader_promises.description: Measure success against casualties, ethics, and strategic consequence rather than completion alone.

roles.name: Commander
roles.description: Interprets orders while bearing responsibility for people and outcome.

roles.name: Mission specialist
roles.description: Provides a capability whose limitations shape the operation.

roles.name: Dissenter
roles.description: Challenges tactics, authority, purpose, or acceptable cost from within the unit.

stakes: Lives of the unit and civilians

movements.name: Orders and stakes
movements.description: Define objective, intelligence limits, command structure, and wider purpose.

movements.name: Contact
movements.description: Let reality contradict assumptions and force local adaptation.

movements.name: Operational fracture
movements.description: Divide resources, authority, or interpretation at the moment cooperation matters most.

movements.name: Objective choice
movements.description: Resolve what version of mission success the unit will accept and pay for.

complications.name: Faulty intelligence
complications.description: An assumption fails for an attributable operational reason.

complications.name: Civilian presence
complications.description: People outside the mission complicate force, timing, and legitimacy.

complications.name: Command split
complications.description: Two legitimate authorities demand incompatible action.

twists.name: Strategic decoy
twists.description: The unit's task serves a wider operation whose cost was concealed.

twists.name: Parallel enemy duty
twists.description: The opposing unit faces a structurally similar obligation without erasing accountability.

conclusions.name: Mission achieved
conclusions.description: The objective is secured and its human cost receives specific aftermath.

conclusions.name: Tactical win, strategic loss
conclusions.description: Local success worsens the wider conflict or legitimacy.

conclusions.name: Moral refusal
conclusions.description: The unit preserves a deeper duty by altering or abandoning the order.

subversions: Center logistics, medicine, or communication rather than marksmanship.
Let restraint achieve the strategically meaningful victory.
cliches_to_avoid: Disposable teammates introduced only to die
An enemy without objectives, constraints, or adaptive behavior
quality_checks: Each specialist contribution has a limit or cost.
Battle outcomes follow terrain, information, and choices.
Aftermath distinguishes objective completion from moral success.

sources.title: The Team Film Genre
sources.contribution: Analyzes differentiated military teams, preparation, main events, weakness, sacrifice, and coda.

sources.title: Aphorisms for Writing Science Fiction
sources.author_or_organization: Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association
sources.contribution: Supports motivated action, consistent scale, thematic climax, and dramatic economy.
